## What Marathon is

Marathon is a science-fiction survival extraction first-person shooter developed by the team behind Halo and Destiny.{{cite:marathon-official-site}} In the game, players assume the role of bio-cybernetic Runners who enter the derelict settlements and installations on Tau Ceti IV to locate valuable gear while contending with UESC forces, other players, and hazardous locales.{{cite:bungie-press-mid-season-2}}{{cite:marathon-official-site}} Runners inhabit configurable biosynthetic bodies called Runner shells, each founded on a distinct gameplay archetype that shapes playstyle and strategy.{{cite:bungie-runner-shells}}

## Release, platforms, and editions

Marathon launched on March 5, 2026.{{cite:bungie-server-slam}} The game is available in Standard and Deluxe editions and was released on Steam as well as on PlayStation 5 and the Xbox Series consoles. It supports cross-play and cross-save.{{cite:bungie-press-mid-season-2}}{{cite:bungie-server-slam}}

## Price and purchase

Pre-ordering granted extra in-game items and platform-linked bonuses, such as exclusive weapon charms for PlayStation 5 players with PlayStation Plus at release.{{cite:bungie-server-slam}}

## Core loop and live service

Seasons run roughly three months and deliver free, seasonal content updates that add zones, Runner shells, gameplay systems, and other features to the live game.{{cite:bungie-introducing-seasons}} In a November 2026 patch, Bungie introduced Expedition, a permanent cooperative PvE roguelite mode available across multiple zones.{{cite:bungie-expedition-phase-1}}

bodyMarkdown:
## What Marathon is

Marathon is a science-fiction survival extraction first-person shooter developed by Bungie, whose prior work includes Halo and Destiny.{{cite:marathon-official-site}}{{cite:pcgamer-review}} Players perform contracted runs on the derelict colony at Tau Ceti IV to recover valuables while opposing UESC forces, other Runners, and environmental hazards.{{cite:marathon-official-site}}{{cite:bungie-press-mid-season-2}} Matches support up to 16 participants across the game’s maps and modes.{{cite:pcgamer-review}} If a Runner is killed during a run, the loot they carried for that sortie is lost unless they successfully exfiltrate.{{cite:pcgamer-guide}} 

Runners inhabit configurable biosynthetic bodies known as Runner shells, each designed around a distinct gameplay archetype and customisable via cores, implants, weapons, and mods.{{cite:bungie-runner-shells}} Six shells are available at launch, among them the Thief frame.{{cite:bungie-introducing-seasons}}

## Release, platforms, and editions

Marathon launched on March 5, 2026.{{cite:bungie-server-slam}} It is offered in Standard and Deluxe editions on PlayStation 5, on the Xbox Series consoles, and on Steam. Cross-play is supported, as is cross-save.{{cite:bungie-press-mid-season-2}}{{cite:bungie-server-slam}} The game’s initial standard price was forty US dollars.{{cite:pcgamer-guide}}

## Price and purchase

Pre-ordering granted in-game bonuses and platform-specific items, including PS5 PlayStation Plus weapon charms at launch.{{cite:bungie-server-slam}}{{cite:bungie-press-symbiosis}} Pre-order incentives included cosmetics, an emblem, a player background, and linked rewards for Destiny 2 via Bungie.net.{{cite:bungie-server-slam}}

## Core loop and live service

Seasons run for roughly three months and deliver free updates that add zones, Runner shells, systems, and other gameplay elements.{{cite:bungie-introducing-seasons}} Seasonal progression resets keep certain long-term unlocks such as cosmetics and Codex entries while restarting core progression and contracts each season.{{cite:bungie-introducing-seasons}} 

A permanent cooperative PvE roguelite mode called Expedition was added in a November 2026 update; it provides a dedicated PvE queue for multi-run series spanning several zones and introduces in-run upgrades called Flash Boosts.{{cite:bungie-expedition-phase-1}}{{cite:bungie-press-symbiosis}} Expedition’s Phase 1 includes Run Series consisting of three consecutive runs with escalating difficulty and rewards.{{cite:bungie-expedition-phase-1}}

## Overview

Marathon features six factions: CyberAcme, Arachne, Sekiguchi Genetics, MIDA, Traxus, and NuCaloric.{{cite:pcgamer-guide}}

## Unlocking factions and contracts

Factions become available after completing liaison contracts, which enable reputation and further contracts for that faction.{{cite:gamesradar-factions}}

## Reputation and upgrades

Completing contracts grants faction reputation used to unlock seasonal upgrades, stronger base stats, and Armory wares.{{cite:bungie-introducing-seasons}} Each season provides a clean slate with progression resets for faction ranks, while liaison contract progress carries over.{{cite:bungie-introducing-seasons}} Season 2 moved many Runner shell upgrades into the Cradle and introduced unique implant families per faction.{{cite:bungie-welcome-season-2}}

## UESC as antagonist

The derelict UESC Marathon serves as the site for end-game Cryo Archive content aboard the ship.{{cite:bungie-server-slam}} UESC combatants appear during runs and were tuned by Bungie to adjust their health and combat impact (Update 1.0.0.4, March 11, 2026).{{cite:bungie-update-1-0-0-4}}

## Overview

Marathon includes six factions that issue contracts to Runners: CyberAcme, Arachne, Sekiguchi Genetics, MIDA, Traxus, and NuCaloric.{{cite:pcgamer-guide}}

## Unlocking factions and contracts

Factions are unlocked by completing a faction's liaison contract, which ONI issues once the player has progressed far enough; finishing that liaison enables the player to earn reputation with that faction and take on its full suite of contracts.{{cite:gamesradar-factions}} Priority contracts are single‑use, story‑important missions that grant higher‑value loot such as Marathon weapons, backpacks, and Salvage.{{cite:gamesradar-factions}} Standard contracts are repeatable challenges that award reputation and routine rewards; players can only hold one standard contract at a time and may spend Credits to reroll it.{{cite:gamesradar-factions}}

## Reputation and upgrades

Completing contracts generates faction reputation, which is spent to unlock seasonal faction upgrades, improved baseline statistics, and new items in the Armory.{{cite:bungie-introducing-seasons}} Seasonal upgrades grant passive benefits such as enhanced starting equipment, expanded vault capacity, and faction‑specific Armory inventory.{{cite:marathon-official-site}} Each season begins with progression resets for most systems, but liaison contract progress persists between seasons.{{cite:bungie-introducing-seasons}} Season 2 relocated many Runner shell upgrade nodes into a new Cradle system and added distinct implant families for each faction, including separate head, torso, and leg implant tracks.{{cite:bungie-welcome-season-2}}

## UESC as antagonist

The derelict UESC Marathon serves as the setting for Cryo Archive content, an end‑game zone that becomes reachable during Season 1.{{cite:bungie-server-slam}}{{cite:bungie-introducing-seasons}} UESC combatants appear during runs and received tuning changes in Update 1.0.0.4 (March 11, 2026), which lowered most UESC enemy health by roughly 10–15% and reduced UESC boss shield HP by 25%.{{cite:bungie-update-1-0-0-4}}

title: Runner shells
summary: Overview of Marathon's Runner shells, how cores and implants differ, the roster across seasons, and former codenames.
bodyMarkdown:
## What Runner shells are

Runner shells are moddable biosynthetic bodies that house player consciousness for survival on Tau Ceti.{{cite:bungie-runner-shells}} Runner shells provide diverse playstyle foundations for scavenging moddable weapons, implants, and core upgrades.{{cite:marathon-official-site}} Rook is a frame designed for scavenger mode, letting a solo player join in-progress matches without risking a loadout.{{cite:bungie-runner-shells}}

## Cores versus implants

Cores are generally tied to one specific Runner shell and modify how that shell’s abilities function.{{cite:bungie-runner-shells}} Implants are universal across Runner shells and provide stats plus a random perk, with high-tier implants granting a bonus fixed perk.{{cite:bungie-runner-shells}} Season 2 changed implants to be defined by perk first and have fixed stats, with names reflecting their perks.{{cite:bungie-welcome-season-2}}

## Roster and seasons

Bungie announced Sentinel as a new Season 2 Runner shell built for area control and defensive play.{{cite:bungie-welcome-season-2}} Bungie announced Bishop as a new Runner shell arriving with the Symbiosis update, focused on fast, surgical melee bursts.{{cite:bungie-nightfall-refresh}}

## Former codenames

Community sources list Thief, Triage, Vandal, Recon, Assassin, Destroyer, and Rook with former or informal codenames Glitch, Blackbird, Void, Locus, and others.{{cite:marathonwiki-org-runners}}

title: Weapons
summary: This page covers Marathon's launch weapons by class and ammo type, general weapon systems, ammo economy, and post-launch weapon additions and balance changes.
bodyMarkdown:
## Overview

Marathon debuted with a catalog of 28 firearms alongside a complete set of mods, implants, and cores for players to craft builds.{{cite:bungie-introducing-seasons}} The initial arsenal covers the usual combat categories—examples include assault-style rifles, close‑quarters shotguns and submachine guns, precision and sniper platforms, high-capacity machine guns, railgun chargers, and sidearms—each using one of several ammunition types such as ballistic rounds or energy cells.{{cite:gamesradar-weapons}}

## How weapons, loot, and ammo work

Weapons, weapon chip mods, and other advancement rewards can be obtained through faction progression and Armory offers.{{cite:gamesradar-factions}} Some types of high‑power ammunition are distributed less frequently and have smaller stack sizes, which increases their cost when consumed in combat.{{cite:pcgamer-review}}

## Post-launch weapons and tuning

The KKV-9SD was introduced in Season 2 as a pistol-frame SMG featuring an integrated suppressor; it accepts pistol optics and pistol magazines and is tuned for very high fire rate and close-range engagements.{{cite:bungie-s2-combat-tuning}} The D54 Battle Pistol arrived as a fully automatic three-round-burst handgun meant to operate between pistol and magnum roles and to pair well with folding stock mods.{{cite:bungie-s2-combat-tuning}} Season 2 also implemented a suite of changes to ammo economy, range identities, and weapon roles intended to make archetypes and player choices clearer.{{cite:bungie-s2-combat-tuning}}

Mid‑Season 2 updates provided further balance adjustments, including buffs to the WSTR Combat Shotgun and tuning for the D54 Battle Pistol and the Misriah-2442 shotgun.{{cite:bungie-press-mid-season-2}} Patch 1.1.0.1 (June 9, 2026) addressed multiple issues, among them a bug where rapid input could improperly extend the D54 Battle Pistol Prestige mod effect.{{cite:bungie-update-1-1-0-1}} A later content update announced two additional weapons: the short-range V17 Flamethrower and the Maverick revolver-style hand-cannon.{{cite:bungie-press-symbiosis}}

## Launch weapons

## Overview of a run

Runs take place on Tau Ceti IV and include scavenging, combat, and exfiltration phases.{{cite:marathon-official-site}} Matches are survival extraction encounters featuring both PvP and PvPvE elements.{{cite:marathon-official-site}}

## Infil and loot

Players infil into zones like Perimeter, Dire Marsh, Outpost, and Cryo Archive.{{cite:bungie-vidoc}} Scavenging yields moddable weapons, implants, and core system upgrades for builds.{{cite:marathon-official-site}} Certain high-value loot like Tag Chips count toward Ranked score targets.{{cite:bungie-ranked}}

## PvPvE, death, and penalties

When a runner dies, they lose all carried loot and cannot retrieve it.{{cite:pcgamer-guide}} In Ranked, failing to exfil or dying causes loss of Ranked Points based on Holotag values.{{cite:bungie-ranked}} Holotags set a score target and a loss penalty for a team's run.{{cite:bungie-ranked}}

## Exfil, crews, solo play, and Vaults

Exfil rewards stronger builds by allowing players to keep stolen loot and advance progression.{{cite:marathon-official-site}} The Vault Breaker mode lets players attempt Cryo Archive content solo, in duos, or in trios.{{cite:bungie-press-mid-season-2}}

## Overview of a run

Runs occur on Tau Ceti IV and combine scavenging, combat, and exfiltration phases as part of a survival-extraction format.{{cite:marathon-official-site}} These matches mix player-versus-player interaction with PvPvE encounters.{{cite:marathon-official-site}}

## Infil and loot

Players drop into planetary zones such as Perimeter, Dire Marsh, Outpost, and the UESC Marathon’s Cryo Archive.{{cite:bungie-vidoc}}{{cite:bungie-cryo-archive}} A solo queue option exists so Runners can be matched without bringing a pre-made crew.{{cite:bungie-vidoc}} Scavenged items include moddable firearms, body implants, and core system upgrades that feed into build customization.{{cite:marathon-official-site}} Some Vault Keys required to open Cryo Archive Vaults are obtainable in planet-side content and by eliminating opposing Runner crews.{{cite:bungie-cryo-archive}} While inside Cryo Archive, a run-based Security Clearance progression is used to unlock doors, supply rooms, and certain exfil options.{{cite:bungie-cryo-archive}} High-value items such as Tag Chips contribute to Ranked objectives and behave specially on exfil.{{cite:bungie-ranked}}{{cite:bungie-ranked}}

## PvPvE, death, and penalties

Death causes the immediate loss of carried loot, and that dropped equipment cannot be retrieved by the deceased Runner.{{cite:pcgamer-guide}} In Ranked play, failing to exfil or being killed results in a loss of Ranked Points proportionate to the Holotag values a team carried.{{cite:bungie-ranked}} Holotags establish both the run’s score target and the penalty applied if the team fails to meet extraction requirements.{{cite:bungie-ranked}}

## Exfil, crews, solo play, and Vaults

Successful exfil allows players to retain stolen items and progress their seasonal unlocks and builds.{{cite:marathon-official-site}} On Night Marsh, activating some exfils and high-value containers requires UESC Certs obtained from defeating UESC forces and hacking Network Towers.{{cite:bungie-welcome-season-2}} A fully upgraded personal Vault expands storage capacity up to 512 inventory grid spaces.{{cite:bungie-welcome-season-2}} Vault Breaker is an experimental roguelite PvE mode set inside Cryo Archive that can be entered alone, with one other player, or with a three-person crew.{{cite:bungie-press-mid-season-2}}{{cite:bungie-press-mid-season-2}}

claimSupport.claimText: Entering a Ranked run requires a Holotag, which determines both the run’s score target and the penalty applied for failing to exfil. Holotags remain in a player’s possession after a successful exfil and may be sold for their full credit value following exfil. A Bronze Holotag sets a 3,000 score target and a 600 loss penalty. Silver Holotags set a 5,000 score target and a 2,000 loss penalty. Gold Holotags set a 7,000 score target and a 4,200 loss penalty. Platinum Holotags set a 10,000 score target and an 8,000 loss penalty. Diamond Holotags set a 15,000 score target and a 15,000 loss penalty. Pinnacle Holotags set a 20,000 score target and a 20,000 loss penalty.

claimSupport.claimText: A team’s combined Holotag credit value establishes the score target for that run. Items in a player’s starting loadout are excluded from the score calculation. The loss penalty applied when a team fails to exfil is determined by the team’s combined Holotag value, and RP is deducted only on failed exfils.
